items_missed: No agenda statement at all - jumped straight from 'How can I help you?' into 'what was your target date?' with no roadmap of the call and no 'sound good?' confirmation
No 'pricing is super simple' opener - went straight into the $222 number
No Worries Damage Coverage never mentioned - 'insurance' was named only as a line item inside what's included, with no $2,000 repair/replace/reimburse explanation
No full 'no hidden fees' pitch - only partial credit for 'includes absolutely everything' and 'no fees for rescheduling or canceling'
Never probed packing needs or quoted packing service pricing, despite a 15-25 box one-bedroom
Never asked the moving-stressor question ('anything you're particularly worried about?')
Collected street addresses and unit numbers for all three stops but no zip codes
No 'does that make sense?' sense-check after the clock explanation
Entire Save Your Ass prep speech skipped - no prep-shortens-the-move framing, no consolidation examples, no 'take a carload' tip
No booking attempt - said 'we're pretty much wide open on that booking' but never asked to lock the date in, even after the customer said he was collecting quotes
Confirmation email described only as 'I'll send the price over' - no bolded-details list, no 'reply with any corrections'
No explicit 'any other questions before I let you go?' and no business hours given
Used the customer's name only once ('my pleasure, Sam') in a 13.6-minute call
top_strength: The estimate build was genuinely excellent and transparent - he gave the 2.5-3.5 hour typical range for a one-bedroom, then showed his math out loud for padding to 4.25 hours (100 ft walk at origin, 120 ft assumed at destination, 5-7 min drive to the storage stop, elevators), quoted $943.50, said it 'definitely could come under,' and offered to revise once the customer measures the elevator-to-unit walk. Discovery was also thorough - room-by-room inventory, elevator reservation, drive-up vs. building access at the storage unit.
coaching_note: Chris ran a strong discovery and estimate but sold zero differentiators and never asked for the business - and this was the call to do both on. The customer volunteered 'we're just getting a couple of different quotes right now,' which is the buying signal to counter with No Worries Damage Coverage, Meet Your Mover, the On-Time Guarantee and no deposit, then close with 'we're wide open on the 26th - want me to hold it? There's no deposit and no fee to reschedule.' He already had the no-reschedule-fee line in hand and used it as a fun fact instead of a closing tool. Second priority: the customer literally opened with 'how many hours to ask for' - that is a direct invitation to run the Save Your Ass prep speech (consolidate loose items, take a carload), and it was skipped entirely.
phone_presence_notes: Polite and competent but transactional - long stretches of 'Okay. Okay.' with no affirmations or empathy markers, the customer carried most of the warmth, and Chris only loosened up near the end with 'Absolutely, yeah absolutely' and 'my pleasure, Sam.'
